/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 66-year-old man presents to the office complaining of fatigue. He reports that for the past year he has been experiencing a progressive decrease in energy. This week he began having some difficulty breathing while climbing the stairs. He denies chest pain or palpitations. He has no other chronic medical conditions and has had no prior surgeries. The patient is found to be anemic. A fecal occult blood test is positive, and a colonoscopy is obtained. The patient is subsequently diagnosed with colorectal cancer. He undergoes a partial colectomy and is started on 5-fluorouracil as adjuvant chemotherapy. Which of the following should be monitored as the patient continues treatment?

Options:
A. Creatinine
B. Fecal leukocytes
C. Monofilament testing
D. Neutrophil count
E. Peak flow

text: {"in_scope": false, "reason": "The question pertains to oncology and chemotherapy monitoring, not psychiatry or mental health."}
